items.title: Annie Ross interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001
items.q: But Hamp could still go out and play blues and then you had wonderful soloists like Art Farmer and like Brownie [Clifford Brown].

ctx.x: Well where would a big band — what camp is that going to fall in? That’s going to fall in the bebop camp, isn’t it?

Well the band did, the arrangements did. But Hamp could still go out and play blues and then you had wonderful soloists like Art Farmer and like Brownie [Clifford Brown]. But they wanted a blues shouter and I’m not that.
So what did you decide after that? Back to New York?
